---
title: "Decisions"
---
The decisions that shaped the method, oldest first, under the numbers the data and the documents cite. Decisions about the people and the logistics of the review are summarized.

| id | date | question | options | decision |

| D-011 | 2026-10-07 | Should the source hunt be broadened beyond the Bendix lineage? | Bendix lineage only; all public-domain granular test records usable for simulator validation | Broadened: Apollo era to today; declared scope per release; eligibility graded on rights; data form and setup recoverability |

| D-016 | 2026-10-07 | How are Volume II unnumbered tables and repeated figures indexed? | one row per soil specification; one row per printed table with a page-locator id; repeats dropped | One row per printed table with id TA-pNNN (PDF page); repeated figures and tables kept as rows with relation reproduces and in_scope no and priority 3; relations to Volume I recorded (derived-from and reproduces) |
| D-017 | 2026-10-08 | When does the first paper go out and how does the validation effort split? | data paper after the simulations; data paper as soon as the harvest and website are done; one validation thread; CRM and DEM threads | Data paper as soon as the harvest is reviewed and the website UX is iterated (no simulation result needed); validation then runs as two parallel threads with their own papers: CRM (mu(I) baseline per D-006) and DEM; framing is archaeology of half-century-old test data made public for sim2real |
| D-018 | 2026-10-08 | How are two trace readings sampled at different displacements compared and how wide is a trace bound? | nearest-x matching with x treated as a measurement; interpolate the other reading at the canonical sample and compare y with the slope-propagated x bounds; bound = full line thickness; bound = half the line thickness | Interpolation rule with slope-propagated x bounds; trace bound is half the line thickness (center known to within half the width); one-sided points enter data only as one-sided-verified after the other agent checks the page or stay one-sided; interpolations across visible gaps are excluded |
| D-019 | 2026-10-08 | What does a record page show and where does the maintainers' material go? | one page with everything (status table, reconciliation record, agents' notes, data); user-facing page with the process material collapsed; user-facing page with the process material on a separate provenance page | Record pages carry only what a user of the data needs (summary, trust note, data in SI, reproduce table with as-printed values and per-test-type fields, family, source pages, citation); the reconciliation record, point statuses, calibration residuals, agents' notes and audit status live on review/<record>; scan overlays once per figure on the figures page; persistent ambiguities that matter for reproduction are stated on the page and labeled as our observation; the pilot's wide bounds stay until a re-read after the student audit |
| D-020 | 2026-10-08 | How are student audits organized? | one packet per student with announced checks; unannounced seeded mistakes; single or double review per point | A light starter packet first (8 rows), identical for every student; seeded attention checks in every packet, whose answers are known, never announced and scored before any answer is recorded; every audited point reviewed by two students (four students, six pairs cycled); no time estimate given to students |
| D-021 | 2026-10-09 | How does a checklist row tell the student what to do, and how does the student look closer? | guide only; a question per row in the checklist; value columns kept or dropped; an image viewer to install; a viewer page in the packet | Each checklist row states its question in a 'what to check' column; the value columns (value read, other reading) are dropped because the answer comes from the picture; a compare row is answered in A with blue, orange or cannot tell; compare close-ups show a wider window (3x, 300 scan px) so both curves' symbols are in view; every packet carries viewer.html (the scan in a browser page, offline: pick a row or type pixel x and y to place the crosshair, pixel under the mouse) |
| D-022 | 2026-10-13 | How is the full audit of the digitized figures organized? | one e-mail with everything once all data exists; weekly waves as the data is read; fixed pairs or rotating pairs; 2 or 5 hours a week | Weekly waves, each with the figures read that week and due a week later; every chunk to one pair of reviewers, the pairs cycled so that each person gets about 4 chunks of about 60 rows a week and no fixed partner; seeded attention checks in every chunk; sampling per figure: compare rows (cap 6), all resolved and unverified one-sided points, one-sided-verified points (cap 10), then agreed points round-robin to a quota proportional to the square root of the figure's point count; answer keys never in a packet; scoring chunk by chunk across runs, with a status board. |
| D-023 | 2026-10-13 | How are two curve readings reconciled when they differ in what they cover, and who settles disputed points? | pair markers by sequence or by position; bridge gaps in the other trace under a pixel threshold or verify by eye; compare features by position or by role; keep or drop points only the non-canonical reader recorded; one adjudicator or two blind ones | Markers paired by position on the page; features by role (first, peak, last) and a peak compared in y only with its x bound widened to the other reading; trace samples inside a gap of the other trace stay one-sided and are verified by eye, no bridging rule; points only the non-canonical reader recorded are kept as one-sided with their own source; a one-sided marker on another test's marker in the other reading is an identity conflict; every disputed or one-sided point goes to a blind adjudication packet (neutral labels P and Q), answered independently by a Claude and a Codex adjudicator; agreement settles, the other agent's adjudicator verifies one-sided points, splits go to a second round and then to the human audit |
| D-024 | 2026-10-14 | Five method questions from batches curves-appc-b3 to -b5: calibration of gridless figures, triangle centers, envelope identity, a printed legend error, re-deriving values after a tool fix | residual rule as is or limited to printed anchors; bounding-box center or centroid; line or legend shape for identity; keep or correct a printed legend; re-read or re-derive | A calibration residual counts only against printed marks (detected grid lines or measured ticks); residuals over lines predicted from the frame show internal consistency and cannot win the canonical choice, so a batch may name the canonical reading with its reason (overlays.csv canonical, canonical_reason); a reader who saved a tick map is re-derived on it so both compete on printed marks. Triangle center: the centroid of the reconstructed triangle; until the 1968 registration point is established the bound in the apex direction includes the bounding-box midpoint (height/6); earlier readings with mixed conventions are to be normalized by a documented re-derivation (open). Envelope identity: neither line nor shape decides alone; the data-sheet peaks of the same tests, where they distinguish the candidates, settle it (corroboration from another depiction, not independent validation). A printed legend error is corrected by a canonical-stage series rename with its evidence (series-ids.csv), the submissions and *_printed fields faithful to the print. Values re-derived from a submission's own pixels and calibration after a tool fix are sound and kept under qa/<batch>/rederived/. |
| D-025 | 2026-10-14 | One affine map per panel, or a piecewise map between the drawn lines, on hand-drafted grids that are not uniform? | affine over all lines; affine over the labelled lines only; piecewise linear between verified lines | Piecewise linear between verified scale lines on every panel (no threshold: on a uniform grid it equals the affine map), in the axis's transformed coordinates for log scales, keeping each line's tilt. A frame is a knot only with a supported value (on FC-6B and FC-6D the left frame is x = 0, recorded as inferred: the first lower-panel symbols sit on it); predicted lines and misplaced text are never knots. Bounds propagate the point's pixel interval and the position intervals of its two bracketing lines, with line-location error from independent checks; the global affine residual becomes a diagnostic of the drafting and is no longer added to every point. The two readings' maps are compared at every knot and interval over the plot, not only at four corners, and the canonical reading is chosen by independent line-position validation (tie to the first submission). The affine-minus-piecewise difference is reported as a correlated calibration sensitivity (initial stiffness above all); slope changes at grid lines are not soil behaviour. Existing readings: pixels kept, values re-derived under qa/<batch>/rederived/, reconciliation rerun, ink and identity decisions carried by source and sequence. To be implemented in tools/calibrate_axes.py, diff_curves.py and build_observations.py as one step, then all batches re-derived (open). |
| D-026 | 2026-10-14 | D-025 as implemented: how is a reader's line verified against the page, which reading is canonical when the ink cannot separate the maps, and what happens to earlier decisions when the canonical reading changes? | tie: first submission, previous canonical reader, denser sampling, affine residual; decisions: re-adjudicate everything, carry by neighbourhood, carry through the pairing; line check: median distance, ink-line fit over the line's length | Tie: first submission (Claude), within 0.25 px of mean line distance from the ink; recomputable from the submissions, the page and the recovered lines, unlike the previous reader, and not a measure of sampling effort or of the retired residual. A reader's line is a knot only when the ink supports its whole length (ink at a quarter of its positions, at least 3, over a third of its length, the ink's fitted line within 2 px of it at both ends; a tick on its stubs); lines a reader left out or misplaced are recovered from that reading's own neighbouring lines and recorded in qa/<batch>/knots.csv (29 lines and two frames). Coverage: equal lines, then the ink; a strict superset wins when its shared lines are as close; incomparable coverage goes to review. Bounds move the two bracketing lines to the ends of their intervals exactly. Exclusions are applied to both readings before matching and leave a break in a trace; a swap takes the other reading's whole record (source <reader>-interp for an interpolated trace value); a resolution on a paired marker or feature follows the symbol when the canonical reading changes, a trace verification stays with its exact sample; the other reading's samples in gaps of the canonical trace are kept as one-sided. Maps compared along every line of either reading and every interval midline. The new and newly exposed items go to the blind two-round adjudication. |
| D-027 | 2026-10-15 | How do the curve-reading tools handle log and reciprocal axes (Appendix A grain-size curves on log paper, density charts with unit weight on a reciprocal axis)? | (a) readers pass logarithms or reciprocals as anchor values (the old rule 5); (b) the tool owns the transform: declared per axis, anchors keep printed values, every map works in the plotting coordinate q = T(value); (c) resample the scan into linear coordinates | (b). calibrate_axes.py detect --x-transform/--y-transform (linear, log10, reciprocal) records the transform; detect predicts unlabelled lines at their place in q; the affine fit, the D-025 knots, line recovery and the interpolation of traces in diff_curves work in q; values, bounds and SI are in the printed unit; the read bound is the larger half of the interval mapped back from q (symmetric and conservative), and values whose halves differ by more than 10 percent are counted. Two readings with different transforms are not compared until the axis type is settled from the page. Minor lines of log paper are knots only when their identity is unambiguous. |
| D-028 | 2026-10-15 | Should the data label experiments as calibration data or validation data? | (a) label each experiment's role (element tests for calibration, penetration tests for validation); (b) keep the data agnostic: record facts any split needs and leave the roles to each study | (b). Almost any test can calibrate or validate; the role is a choice made in a particular study for a particular claim with a particular model. The data records, per experiment, what kind of test it is (element, boundary-value, derived series, summary), what was measured and how well (setup completeness, response, uncertainty, repeat-test scatter), and how tests depend on each other (same soil, state, laboratory; same-as, derived-from), plus notes on what a test can and cannot pin down for a given kind of model. Example splits are documented with the benchmark, not in the data. |
| D-029 | 2026-10-15 | Who reviews the audit packets, and at what weekly load? | (a) five reviewers, the project lead included, 4 chunks each; (b) the four student reviewers only, the same 600-row wave sample, 5 chunks each; (c) the four student reviewers at 4 chunks each, a smaller sample | (b). The project lead stays out of the checking. The four student reviewers each take 5 chunks of 60 rows a week. Wave 1 was re-planned before it went out (the sample follows the canonical points as they are now, which had moved since 10-14 for 263 of 600 rows): 10 chunks over the 6 pairs, four pairs twice and two once, 5 chunks per person. |
| D-030 | 2026-10-27 | How are the outcomes of the audit re-check (qa/adjudication-2026-10-27) applied to the data? | apply all (switches, exclusions, widened bounds); apply switches and widened bounds, hold the exclusions; apply nothing until the off-ink rule exists | Switches as decisions with use <other reader> (11); points neither reading could be shown right on keep their value with bounds widened to both readings by a new decision value use span (8 pending-review, 2 resolved); the 48 off-ink trace exclusions are held: excluding a kept sample opens a break, and the other reader's samples in it (3 to 5 per break, at the symbol, where the adjudicators found the other line off the ink too) would enter as about 180 unverified one-sided points. The exclusions wait for the off-ink rule (D-031), which judges both readings' samples. |
| D-031 | 2026-10-27 | How is CURVE-READING rule 7 (a trace sample is on its line's own ink, never on a symbol or in a dash/symbol gap) checked mechanically in every batch? | (a) no ink within 2 px plus a symbol bounding-box footprint (Claude's blind design); (b) ink ownership: fitted symbol-stroke, grid and curve-fragment masks reviewed on the page, distance to the series' own ink normal to the stroke, a three-way gate (eligible, excluded, needs review) with a 1 px perturbation (Codex's blind design) | (b), as tools/check_trace_ink.py v1, applied as is on 2026-10-30 (D-032). |
| D-032 | 2026-10-30 | Is the off-ink check (D-031 v1) applied as it is, improved first, or left in shadow mode? | (a) apply v1 now and disclose what it misses; (b) build v2 for the two miss families first; (c) keep shadow mode | (a). v1 is precise (98 percent of its exclusions are right) and incomplete (about half of the off-ink samples), and a sample it misses is no worse than before; waiting for v2 would hold the 48 adjudicated exclusions of D-030 and every batch after them. Applied: the 48 hand exclusions written (47 new rows, 1 updated, 21 already there), tools/reconcile_curves.py runs the check by default (--no-ink-checks reproduces the readings before it), all 16 curve batches re-derived and their records rebuilt. Effect: 822 trace samples excluded across the diffs, 40 hand decisions overridden (listed in the diff reports); canonical points 9,663 to 9,825 (agreed 8,318 to 7,892; one-sided 163 to 791, the other reading's samples in the breaks, unverified); observation rows 9,589 to 9,751, 58 of 162 records changed; one wave 2 audit row lost its point. The miss families (curve ends at the frame or a grid line, symbol junctions) and the 301 review verdicts are listed in docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md. |
| D-033 | 2026-10-30 | How are the questions the project cannot settle now kept from stalling it? | (a) settle each before moving on; (b) a public list of open questions with a disclaimer, in the repository and on the site, so that anyone can help; nothing waits on a single reviewer or a single question | (b). docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md, rendered on the site as Open questions and linked from the overview, lists every known soft spot with its evidence file and how to help; the overview says the data set is a first step, not a finished product. A consequence for the audit: a point whose second reviewer has not returned stands as checked by one person (its row in qa/audits.csv says so), and no wave waits for it. |
| D-034 | 2026-11-02 | When and how does the data set become public? | (a) at the data paper's submission, as planned (roadmap 7d); (b) now, as a versioned public preview updated as the work goes, open to scrutiny and use, with simulations started in parallel | (b). Public repository uwsbel/terramechanics-reference-data, titled Terramechanics Reference Data, for simulation-to-reality gap analysis; no era in the name, so a physical test run today can join under the same provenance rules. Each release is a fresh tree without history, built by tools/make_public_release.py from a commit of this repository, because the history and the audit files hold the student reviewers' names and e-mail addresses and the answer keys of waves still out: those files stay out, reviewer initials become R1 to R4, and the build fails if a name is left. The tracked source files go in (73 MB), so every page image a reading refers to can be rendered from the release alone. Data CC BY 4.0, code BSD-3-Clause; versioned snapshots (v0.1 first) with CHANGELOG.md and CITATION.cff; a Zenodo DOI later. No sponsor; nothing else gates the release. |
| D-035 | 2026-11-05 | Does the first journal paper carry a simulation, and which one? | (a) a data paper with no simulation result (D-017); (b) one bounded demonstration in the data paper, CRM only; (c) one bounded demonstration with CRM and DEM side by side, each model gated on its own | (c). The paper starts an open collection of traceable terramechanics tests for judging simulation tools and shows the data in use with an open-source simulator. Demonstration: dense RS, 4-inch cylinder, Fig. 2-42 (printed 2-77, PDF 102): calibrate on LPT 24, predict LPT 23, 25 and 22 with the parameters frozen; LPT 74 (Fig. 2-44) only if its setup gaps close in time. Both models in Chrono: CRM with mu(I) (D-006) from demo_<wbr>FSI-SPH_<wbr>PlateSinkage,<wbr> and Chrono::DEM spheres with rolling resistance. The protocol is frozen in benchmark/ before the first prediction run; the gap is split into reading, setup, calibration and numerical parts; every verified result is reported whichever way it falls, an unverified run is not. Claude prepares and runs the virtual experiments on amd-cluster at a pinned Chrono commit; Codex reviews each stage (specification, scripts, verification, calibration, predictions) before Dan sees it. Target: Journal of Terramechanics, submitted 2026-12-18, gates per model on 11-09, 11-18, 11-25 and 12-02 (roadmap 7c); a model that misses 12-02 goes to its own thread paper, and if both miss it the paper goes in by late January 2027. Calibration and validation roles belong to this study, not to the data (D-028). |
| D-036 | 2026-11-05 | How does the audit continue with three reviewers, and what happens to a return that misses an attention check? | Schedule: (a) re-deal the chunks without a return and raise the other reviewers' load; (b) stretch the schedule at the same load. A return that misses a check: (a) accept it; (b) decline it and give its points a second reviewer | Schedule (b): chunks without a return are not re-dealt, and their points stand as checked by one person (D-033). From wave 3 three reviewers take 4 chunks each, 6 chunks of 60 rows a wave; 5 each is not possible, because every chunk needs two reviewers and 3 x 5 is odd. The remaining audit takes longer instead. The return (b): a return that misses an attention check that no error of the packet explains is logged as declined and never recorded, and its points get a second reviewer in a later wave. Wave 3 carries the Section II load-penetration batches curves-s2-b1 and -b2 (no load-penetration figure had had a human check yet) and the 10 void identity questions (qa/audits/voided.csv); Figs. 2-42 and 2-44 follow in wave 4. |
| D-037 | 2026-11-06 | How does wave 3 give a second review to the points of packet 2 that have only one, and what changes in the packets? | Second reviews: (a) one single-review chunk's 60 points to one reviewer, leaving that reviewer a chunk short; (b) the points of the two single-review chunks W2-07 and W2-08 to two reviewers, each as one of the reviewer's 4 chunks. Attention checks on curve rows: (a) keep them as they were; (b) revise them. | (b) and (b). Wave 3: 5 chunks of new points from curves-s2-b1 and -b2 (Figs. 2-29 to 2-34, 2-45 to 2-48), dealt over the pairs of the three reviewers, plus the second-review chunks W3-06 (repeats W2-07) and W3-07 (repeats W2-08); 4 chunks each, due 2026-11-16. A second-review chunk has one reviewer and its own attention checks; a point's outcome combines every reviewer of it. A void in qa/audits/voided.csv applies only to the chunk it was given in, so the second reviews ask the 10 void identity questions again, of another reviewer, on upright pictures. Compare rows take both for any symbol or line, not only a triangle. In W2-08 the identity answers on FC-7B and FC-7C, figures the packet showed upside down, are void (26 more rows in qa/audits/voided.csv, 32 in all for that chunk); its location answers and its FC-1A answers stand, and the second review W3-07 asks the identity questions again. |
| D-038 | 2026-11-06 | Is the simulation specification approved, and which DEM code runs the demonstration? | Specification: approve or revise. CRM interfaces: (a) accept CRM's no-slip walls and bodies as a stated limitation; (b) add a friction boundary to CRM first. DEM: (a) Chrono::DEM, as planned; (b) DEM-Engine v2.4.2 on amd-cluster; (c) DEM-Engine 3 on the NVIDIA lab machines; (d) restore HIP in DEM-Engine 3 first. | Specification approved (paper/notes/sim-spec.md): calibrate on LPT 22 to 25 together; hold out LPT 73 (same box) and LPT 74, 69, 64A (larger bins) as conditional predictions; compare total reaction against penetration over 5 to 50 mm with the admissibility rule and verdicts of its section 6; at most 200 node-hours. CRM (a), with the limitation filed as projectchrono/chrono#866 after a check by Codex (gpt-6-astra). DEM (b): DEM-Engine v2.4.2, the last release with the ROCm/HIP backend (DEM-Engine PRs 69 and 77), built on amd-cluster; a short DEM-Engine issue on DEME 3 lacking that backend is drafted for Dan. Replaces the test design of D-035 and Chrono::DEM in PLAN.md B2.4.1. |
| D-039 | 2026-11-07 | How are the adjudication decisions corrected that came from run answers of some, which the apply tool misread? | (a) re-run every affected adjudication from round 1; (b) transcribe each some comment sample by sample (two independent transcriptions, diffed), recompute the affected items with the tool's rules, and correct only the decision rows that came from them; (c) send the affected samples to a new adjudication round | (b). apply_adjudication3.py and apply_adjudication4.py (and the older apply_adjudication.py and apply_adjudication2.py) took every pixel pair in a some comment as an off-line sample, including the samples the comment called on the line, so samples both adjudicators had accepted were excluded or split. First part, 2026-11-07: the 48 some answers of the 7 rounds applied with apply_adjudication3/4 (adjudications of 2026-10-15 and 2026-11-07); Claude and Codex transcribed all 99 samples independently and agreed on every one (48 off, 49 on, 2 unclear). correct_some_answers.py changed 29 rows in 16 decision files: 26 samples now verified (19 had been excluded, 7 left undecided) and 3 back to undecided (one adjudicator on, one off); a sample with no row gets a corrected decision only if no later round decided it. Affected batches reconciled and their records rebuilt (15 figures, 15 records with point changes). Second part, 2026-11-07: the 103 some answers of the six older rounds (curves-appc-b1 rounds 1 and 2, curves-appc-b3 round 1, curves-rederivation-d025 rounds 1 to 3). Claude and Codex transcribed the 261 samples independently and differed on 3, where one adjudicator wrote that a sample lay 1 px from a dash end at line height (Claude's reading on, Codex's unclear); the same adjudicator answered all yes for such samples in items 182 and 184, so on (no decision depends on it): 144 off, 116 on, 1 unclear. These second rounds re-asked only the samples the misread first round had split, and the rounds were merged with the first decision kept, so correct_some_older.py replays the eight rounds of the three chains in order with both readings and gives each affected sample the decision of the latest round that decides it. 58 samples change outcome in some round; 43 rows changed in 9 decision files, one for one the 43 discrepancies Codex had listed: 33 samples now verified (32 had been excluded, 1 left undecided) and 10 back to undecided. With this, all 151 some answers are corrected. Every apply tool (apply_adjudication.py to apply_adjudication4.py) now reads the round's off-lists.csv and never the comment's pixels: a some answer with no transcription leaves the item undecided, and an unclear sample leaves that sample split (until the second part, the whole item: the same decisions in the first part's rounds, while in the older rounds the whole-item rule would also leave undecided the other four samples of curves-appc-b1 round 1 item 068, one verified and three excluded by both adjudicators). Records of the second part rebuilt: 23 records, 40 points added (32 verified, 8 back to one-sided; 2 more stay out by the off-ink check), 24 removed (the other reading's samples that had filled the gaps the wrong exclusions left, one of them confirmed by the student audit), 1 agreed point now one-sided (FC-2C n1468, by the comparison's segment rule); no value changed. |
| D-040 | 2026-11-14 | After the 11-08 diagnostics, does DEM stay in the paper, and how is the CRM virtual experiment set up? | DEM: (a) report the sphere shortfall as a negative result; (b) leave the paper and continue as its own thread with clumps of spheres. CRM: (a) keep mu_2 = mu_s, E 5 to 120 MPa, a physical-speed check with save-and-resume; (b) mu_2 = mu_s + 0.2 and I0 0.08, E about 1 to 20 MPa, a speed check at 10, 20 and 40 mm/s. | DEM (b): DEM leaves the 12-18 paper and becomes its own thread (roadmap 8c) with clumps of spheres, starting from the lab's plate-sinkage campaign and the GRC_DEM work; the sphere runs of 11-07 and 11-08 repeat those findings and are not results of this study. CRM (b): mu_2 = mu_s + 0.2, I0 = 0.08 (the validated example of Chrono's mu(I) manual); E search range about 1 to 20 MPa; the speed check runs faster than 10 mm/s instead of at the physical speed, so no save-and-resume is written. Codex reviews the change before any run; chrono-rag is consulted for every Chrono behavior. |
| D-041 | 2026-11-14 | After the lessons of the lab's KSC CRM study and plate-sinkage campaign, and the stage A screening, how is the CRM demonstration set up? | (a) continue the D-040 design (E 1 to 20 MPa searched, 10 mm/s, 7.5 mm, fp32, comparison 5 to 50 mm); (b) the plan Claude negotiated with Codex in four rounds on 2026-11-14 | (b). Free-surface threshold 2.4 as the baseline, 0.8 reported as a treatment sensitivity. E calibrated jointly with mu_s as an effective stiffness on 5 to 52 MPa (exploratory bounds informed by AM-68-1 Vol. II App. B: the wave modulus with the report's Poisson correction, Eq. 2, PDF 106, and its warning that static and wave moduli differ by about an order of magnitude, PDF 104). mu_s calibrated directly on 0.5 to 1.2 with the yield convention stated; mu_2 - mu_s 0.30 and I0 0.30 as an empirical baseline. Compared quantity: the loading branch and first peak (about 5 to 25 mm), interval and peak rule frozen from the measured curves before fitting, tolerance recomputed, post-peak reported as numerically sensitive. Speed ladder downward (5, 2.5, 1.25 mm/s) from saved beds. 5 mm spacing as the candidate reference with a finer check; three independent beds per condition. Bed prepared once, saved and reloaded, with a vertical-stress and force-balance gate. fp64 for anything quoted. Mid-push checkpoint and restart in lpt_crm, verified against uninterrupted runs, so 4 h partitions can serve; a longer job limit requested from the cluster administrators in parallel.
